titles.title: Plaque depicting a procession to an altar

texts.textentryhtml: The rectangular bronze plaque shows three men processing toward a masonry altar. All three wear short chitons, a type of light tunic, and carry branches over their left shoulders. The first man holds a cup in his right hand while the other two grasp flowers. Facing them on the step of the altar is a flute player, an aulete, who wears a longer robe and a strap, known as a phorbeia, to hold the aulos, the double flute, in his mouth. Behind him, on top of the altar, is a bronze tripod with lion’s paw feet and three ring handles. The ceremony is certainly ritual in nature, but it is unclear what it will entail and to which god it is directed, though the tripod may indicate a connection with Apollo.
Said to have been found near Mylasa, in Caria, a region of southwest Turkey; acquired by Robert Hecht Jr. at an unknown date and from an unknown source; purchased by the Museum in 1999.
